anomaly_def.Name: Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Definition: The system concurrently exhibits on-disk data/index corruption and depletion or instability of network and connection-handling resources, so that storage-layer integrity faults coexist with transport-layer bottlenecks while the same workload is executing.

Combined Anomalous Phenomena: Users may observe intermittent or persistent query failures in the form of checksum or logical-corruption errors interleaved with connection-establishment timeouts and sudden session drops. Index probes can miss or duplicate rows, forcing the optimizer to fall back to full scans that inflate result-set sizes; these larger result streams exacerbate already congested network paths, leading to prolonged client-read waits, retransmissions, and spikes in application latency. Monitoring may show mismatches between heap and index row counts, rising physical-corruption alerts, simultaneous surges in refused or half-open sockets, and database backends stalled in client I/O while error logs report page verification failures.

Causal Interaction: Storage corruption can elongate or repeatedly restart query execution, amplifying the number of concurrent sessions and the volume of data sent over the network, thereby exhausting listener backlogs, socket buffers, or connection pool limits. Conversely, chronic network stalls, abrupt disconnects, and retry storms can interrupt write-ahead flushes or crash ongoing index rebuilds, increasing the likelihood of torn pages and orphaned index entries. Together, these feedback loops degrade both the physical integrity of data structures and the reliability of client connectivity, making recovery and diagnosis significantly more complex and prolonging overall service disruption.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for a block to be written to a connection before aborting the write.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits longer than net_write_timeout while writing a block to the client connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
